canonical_statement: The review examines pro-inflammatory effects of chemotherapy, tumor-promoting effects of inflammation across cancer development, and whether inflammation may contribute to recurrence after chemotherapy.

The review describes chemotherapy-induced accelerated senescence as a route to a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) containing inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and matrix metalloproteinases that may increase chronic inflammation in the tumor microenvironment.

source_anchor.paragraph: Certain chemotherapy drugs can increase inflammation in the TME, paragraph 1

concept.text: SASP-associated inflammatory signaling in the tumor microenvironment

canonical_statement: Table 1 summarizes doxorubicin as linked to SASP production, ZAK-dependent JNK/MAPK inflammatory cytokine production, and NF-kB activation.
Table 1 summarizes cisplatin as linked to TNF-alpha and IL-1beta production, ROS generation, and p38-MAPK/NF-kB-associated pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion.
Table 1 summarizes paclitaxel as linked to increased IL-1beta, IL-8, IL-6 and VEGF-A, activation of TLR4/NLRP3/inflammasome pathways, and NF-kB activation.

outcome.definition: IL-1beta; IL-8; IL-6; VEGF-A; TLR4; NLRP3; NF-kB

canonical_statement: Table 1 summarizes 5-fluorouracil as linked to NF-kB activation and production of inflammatory cytokines including TNF-alpha, IL-1beta and IL-6.
Table 1 summarizes carboplatin as linked to increased serum TNF-beta and induction of NF-kB and inflammatory-cytokine gene expression.
Table 1 summarizes etoposide as linked to NF-kB activation, pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and ROS production.
Table 1 summarizes daunorubicin as linked to IL-1beta release and NLRP3/inflammasome activation.
Table 1 summarizes cyclophosphamide as linked to NF-kB activation and inflammatory cytokine production including TNF-alpha, IL-1beta and IL-6.
Table 1 summarizes mitomycin C as linked to NF-kB activation, inflammatory cytokine production, and ROS generation.

The supplementary figure integrates etoposide, paclitaxel, cisplatin, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, 5-fluorouracil, daunorubicin, carboplatin and mitomycin C with inflammatory signaling through TLR4, NF-kB, MAPK, NLRP3, senescence/SASP and IL-1beta-related pathways.

The review states that chronic inflammation can influence tumor initiation, development and dissemination through immune-cell recruitment, cytokine/chemokine generation, and signaling pathways including NF-kB and STAT3.
The review reports that approximately 5-10% of patients with inflammatory bowel disease develop colon cancer after 20 years and 10-12% after 30 years.

The review reports that approximately 50-70% of patients with lung cancer have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and discusses chronic inflammation and oxidative stress as shared mechanistic links.

The review describes gastroesophageal reflux disease as a risk factor for esophageal cancer through local NF-kB activation, inflammatory cytokine production, ROS-mediated epithelial damage, and chronic inflammatory injury.

canonical_statement: The review links chronic viral hepatitis and chronic alcohol exposure to persistent hepatic inflammation, tissue injury, fibrosis/cirrhosis, and increased possibility of liver cancer.

source_anchor.paragraph: Inflammatory disease and cancer, liver paragraph

canonical_statement: For tumor initiation, the review proposes that ROS/RNS can promote DNA damage and mutations, persistent nitric oxide can impair DNA repair, and inflammatory signaling can support survival of transformed cells.
The review describes STAT3/JAK2-associated epigenetic changes, including DNMT1 activation and methylation of tumor-suppressor promoters, as one proposed inflammation-linked route to carcinogenesis.

source_anchor.paragraph: Inflammation and tumor initiation, final paragraph

canonical_statement: The review identifies inflammatory mediators including ROS, STAT3, NF-kB, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, IL-6, COX-2 and PGE2 as contributors to angiogenesis through HIF-1 and/or direct induction of pro-angiogenic factors such as VEGF.

The review describes inflammation-associated EMT and metastasis through neutrophil/monocyte-derived factors, MMPs, adhesion and vascular-permeability changes, and signaling involving NF-kB, STAT3, ROS and PGE2.

Figure 1 maps inflammatory mediators to cancer initiation, angiogenesis, EMT and metastasis, including ROS/RNS DNA damage, HIF-1/VEGF angiogenic signaling, MMP/adhesion changes and EMT transcription-factor activation.
Table 2 organizes ROS, PGE2, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, NF-kB and STAT3 across proposed roles in cancer initiation, angiogenesis, EMT/metastasis and tumor promotion.

The review describes inflammatory signaling as capable of promoting cancer progression through immune suppression, increased tumor-cell proliferation and inhibition of apoptosis, with STAT3 and NF-kB as central pathways.

The review describes cancer stem cells as relatively chemotherapy-resistant through ABC transporters, ALDH activity, anti-apoptotic proteins, stemness pathways, DNA-repair capacity and G0 cell-cycle latency.

The review proposes that NF-kB, STAT3 and PGE2 can promote cancer-stem-cell survival/self-renewal and that inflammatory cytokines can induce EMT/stemness transcription factors, potentially contributing to relapse.

The review describes MDSC recruitment by inflammatory mediators as suppressing T-cell, CTL and NK-cell function and creating an immunosuppressed environment in which residual cancer stem cells may resume proliferation.

canonical_statement: Figure 2 synthesizes chemotherapy escape by cancer stem cells with inflammatory signaling, immune suppression and self-renewal pathways as a proposed route to recurrence.

The review states that chemotherapy effects on immunity depend on drug, dose and schedule: maximum tolerated doses may cause broad immune suppression, whereas lower doses may reduce inhibitory cells and increase effector-cell responses.

source_anchor.paragraph: The effects of chemotherapy on the adaptive immune system

canonical_statement: Low-dose cyclophosphamide is described as reducing IL-10/TGF-beta-producing regulatory cells while increasing effector cells and shifting macrophage responses toward an M1 phenotype.

exposures.details: low-dose regimen as described by the review

canonical_statement: The review describes several chemotherapy classes as capable of inducing immunogenic cell death through ER-stress-associated calreticulin exposure, ATP release and downstream inflammasome/immune activation, with additional danger signals including HMGB1, HSP70, HSP90 and type I interferons.

source_anchor.paragraph: Adaptive immune section, immunogenic cell death paragraph

canonical_statement: The review notes that mitomycin C can induce conventional apoptosis without the same immune response, while local melphalan plus TNF-alpha can provoke inflammatory mediators and inflammatory-cell recruitment that may promote tumor progression through NF-kB signaling.

The review states that multiple chemotherapy drugs can increase tumor-cell PD-L1 expression and suggests that combining such chemotherapy with anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibodies may improve treatment effects.

The authors hypothesize that chemotherapy-induced chronic inflammation may contribute to treatment inefficiency and relapse, and that concurrent anti-inflammatory therapy could improve outcomes in some cancers, but they explicitly call for preclinical and clinical validation.
